brief: GS's prior note (end of August) argued for AI/semis upside and a bullish SPX framework, based on low implied vol and low AI positioning plus macro uncertainty pushing risk into AI. The desk now says that asymmetry has shifted: macro is harder, and AI/large-cap tech positioning is no longer a tailwind. Since Aug 27, SPX is up 1.28% while SPXXAI (S&P ex the AI names) is down 5.19%, the widest divergence since January 2023. The view branches: either macro (rates, oil) turns friendlier and upside broadens to the rest of the index, or macro stays messy and large-cap tech/AI stall with everything else; the desk now prefers broad-market upside (SPXXAI Nov 102% calls) over AI-specific trades. Tech/AI positioning has risen over 6-8 weeks (Mag7 exposure near 22%, the highest since 2022; semis near 12% vs a 14% June peak), but overall market net positioning stays low (2nd percentile on L/S nets), which the desk argues should contain broad dips. The clearest left-tail risk is a hot CPI forcing the Fed past its priced 5bp October hike, which would hit all sectors near-term.
